title: Police ID man who died after scuffle with transit guards
article: RCMP have identified a man they said behaved erratically on a bus and later died in a hospital in Surrey, B.C.

Ryan Wagemans, 24, of Langley, was arrested Friday evening after he became involved in a struggle with two transit security guards, Cpl. Dale Carr of the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team said Wednesday.
"Investigators are currently reviewing statements and establishing additional contacts in order to determine just what caused Ryan to go into medical distress," Carr said.
Wagemans might have been on a 321 bus prior to getting off and entering the 319 at the Newton bus loop, Carr said.
Investigators are asking anyone on board either of the buses who saw Wagemans behaving strangely to contact police.
The 319 bus driver noticed what police described as Wagemans's "erratic behaviour" and requested help from Coast Mountain Bus Service security guards, Surrey RCMP Sgt. Roger Morrow said Tuesday.
A struggle ensued shortly after two security guards boarded the bus, forcing the vehicle to stop on 72nd Avenue, west of 134th Street.
Surrey RCMP were called to the scene and arrested Wagemans. He went into medical distress and was taken to Surrey Memorial Hospital. He was listed in critical condition and died at 1:25 p.m. Tuesday.
It is the second time in two weeks that a person has died after being arrested by Surrey RCMP.
David James Stitt, 46, died in hospital on June 20, two days after he was arrested by RCMP officers in south Surrey.
Stitt was waving a stick in the 13500 block of Crescent Road when a female RCMP officer answered a call about a disturbance, police said at the time.
The officer used a baton and pepper-sprayed Stitt while attempting to subdue the agitated man, police said.
